basic_info.main_problem: I tend to belittle my achievements, especially the awards I won in ballet, which makes me feel inadequate and lowers my evaluation of success. Especially noticeable when receiving praise or recognition, affecting my self-worth and motivation.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to no longer belittle my achievements, to view and appreciate my success more comprehensively and realistically, improving my sense of self-worth and Learning motivation.
growth_experiences: Family of origin information: only Female child, Mother is a Sunday school teacher (other family members and growing-up events Not mentioned).
Has won awards in ballet (specific times and dates Not mentioned).

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of recognition

special_situations.event: Praised and recognized by others after winning a ballet award
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not top-tier or perfect, it is not worthy of recognition; others' praise may just be politeness rather than genuine evaluation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Quickly Displacing topics, downplaying or negating achievements, attributing success to luck
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just luck, anyone could do it; they are just being polite

special_situations.event: Receiving affirmation after getting Good grades on nursing exams
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not full marks or far surpassing others, it means not good enough and not worthy of self-affirmation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Deliberately belittling grades, not allowing oneself to stay in positive experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is nothing; never good enough

special_situations.event: Friends or peers express appreciation for one's contribution to the team
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are better than me, my contribution is insignificant
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Comparing others' strengths and negating one's own worth, reducing self-expression
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Someone is always better; my contribution is not important

special_situations.event: In a high-pressure period of balancing nursing studies, personal life, and ballet training
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep all areas to high standards, it means I lack ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifies self-berating, downplays progress and achievements made
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not deserve this praise; not worthy of recognition

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be genuinely seen and recognized, expecting one's efforts and achievements to be fairly evaluated
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as undeserving of recognition, being exposed as 'just luck', worrying about others' evaluations and negating oneself
defense_goal: Maintaining humility and safety by negating or downplaying achievements, avoiding exposing the Anxiety of 'not deserving'

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough achiever/Student, prone to Self-deprecation
object_relations.object_representation: Others are polite praisers or potential harsh critics

object_relations.self_representation: A person whose contributions in relationships are insufficient
object_relations.object_representation: Praise from peers and mentors toward oneself is unreliable / may just be perfunctory

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others praise one's ballet award or academic performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' praise as insincere politeness, believing one's success relies on luck (transference: Projecting the inner 'sense of not deserving' onto others' intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle and Empathy tone, using open-ended Questioning to explore effort and evidence, avoiding direct refutation; inviting concrete examples to connect actual effort with results.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites one to stay with the positive feeling of being praised
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding staying in positive experiences as discomfort and danger, worrying about exposing 'not being good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inviting naming of feelings in a low-intensity, gradual way, using brief staying exercises and safety boundaries, gradually expanding tolerance for positive experiences.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When Learning and life Increased stress and affirmation from others is needed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tying self-worth to high standards, believing anything short of perfect is 'not good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reducing abstract judgments, shifting to concrete and present-experience descriptions; encouraging identification of behavioral evidence of effort, connecting emotions and facts in a gentle tone.

manifestations: Diminished sense of meaning about ballet awards and academic grades, believing 'this is nothing / just luck / anyone could do it'
Struggling to stay in self-affirming experiences, tending to downplay and deny positive self-narratives
outcomes: Interpersonal relationships affected (worsened interactions with classmates and mentors)

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Quickly Displacing topics when receiving praise
Not lingering on positive feedback, avoiding present positive experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judging oneself by the high standard of 'must be better / never enough'
Treats perfectionist standards as the only criterion for being recognized

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively harsh on one's own contributions and achievements
Underestimates self-worth in relationships, cautious to the point of finding it hard to accept positive feedback

positive_force: Performance in nursing studies is acceptable (satisfied with academic functioning)
Has won awards in ballet, with dedication and skill
Close relationships with friends, potential support resources exist
Proactively seeks counseling and is willing to try change (motivation and openness)
negative_force: Tending to negate and belittle positive results (Disqualifying the Positive)
Self-demands are too high; black-and-white standards and frequent comparison
Feeling uncomfortable and avoiding when praised (quickly Displacing topics)
Increased academic and life stress, leading to impaired self-care and Decline in sense of well-being

target_behavior.behavior: Automatically belittling and denying self-achievements when accomplishing or being praised (e.g. calling it luck, quickly Displacing topics)
antecedent: Being praised by others after winning a ballet award
Getting Good grades on nursing exams and receiving affirmation
Friends or peers express appreciation for one's contributions
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by the core belief of 'I am not good enough / not worthy of recognition' and high-standard comparisons, avoiding positive self-evaluation to prevent exposing the Anxiety of 'not deserving'
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncomfortable emotions and the feeling of being evaluated, maintaining surface safety and humility
target_behavior.consequence: Self-worth and Decreased drive, affected Interpersonal relationships, lowered self-care and Overall happiness
